---
title: "02 Resistance surface"
output: html_notebook
editor_options:
  chunk_output_type: console
---

Builds the national resistance surface. Starts from the LCM land-cover
classification, adds the NFI woodland layer (a cell is woodland if either
LCM or NFI classes it so) and assigns a resistance value to each
land-cover class. Also fetches the ONS Major Towns and Cities boundaries
used to identify the designated places in each region. Loads
`urban_regions_named` and `nfi_urban` from their saved checkpoints, so it
does not depend on `01b_Analyse_Urban_Regions.Rmd` having been run in the
same session.

```{r setup}
source(here::here("scripts", "00_setup.R"))
```

# Load checkpoints

Loads the named urban regions and the clipped NFI woodland polygons saved by `01b`.

```{r load_checkpoints}
library(sf)

urban_regions_named <- readRDS(
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "07b_urban_regions_named.rds")
)

nfi_urban <- readRDS(
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "nfi_urban_regions.rds")
)

cat("urban_regions_named:", nrow(urban_regions_named), "regions\n")
cat("nfi_urban:", nrow(nfi_urban), "features\n")
```

# National LCM base layer (full classification)

Crops the national LCM raster to the urban-regions extent and aggregates
it from 10 m to 200 m cells (modal resampling), because full detail is
not visible at country scale and is slow to crop and plot nationally.
All LCM classes are kept, not just woodland, because the resistance
surface assigns a value to every class. The NFI woodland is added in the
next chunk. Increase `agg_factor` for a coarser, faster layer.

This chunk and the next (`national_lcm_nfi_classified`) are the slow part
of the notebook: they crop, aggregate and rasterise the NFI over England.
Both load `lcm_nfi_classified.tif` if it already exists, so later chunks
can be re-run without them. Delete that file (or the whole
`checkpoint_dir`) to force a rebuild after changing `agg_factor`, the
woodland rule or the source data.

```{r national_lcm_woodland_base}
library(terra)

agg_factor <- 20  # 10m x 20 = 200m cells

lcm_classified_checkpoint <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "lcm_nfi_classified.tif")

if (file.exists(lcm_classified_checkpoint)) {

  cat("lcm_nfi_classified checkpoint found -- skipping national LCM crop/aggregate (loaded in the next chunk instead).\n")

} else {

  urban_regions_bbox_sfc <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(urban_regions_named))

  cat("Cropping national LCM to the urban-regions extent...\n")

  t_lcm_crop <- system.time({
    lcm_national <- rast(lcm_file) |>
      crop(vect(urban_regions_bbox_sfc))
  })

  print(t_lcm_crop)

  cat("Aggregating from 10m to", agg_factor * 10, "m cells...\n")

  t_lcm_agg <- system.time({
    lcm_national_agg <- aggregate(lcm_national[[1]], fact = agg_factor, fun = "modal")
  })

  print(t_lcm_agg)

}
```

# National LCM + NFI classified map (full classification, woodland patched)

Keeps every LCM class as it is, except that all woodland (LCM class 1,
broadleaved, and class 2, coniferous, plus any cell NFI flags as
woodland) is merged into a single class, 1 "Woodland". Once a cell is
woodland its source does not matter, so this is a union of the two
sources rather than a replacement of one by the other. Urban region
boundaries are overlaid for context.

```{r national_lcm_nfi_classified}
library(terra)

woodland_code <- 1
lcm_present_vals_checkpoint <- file.path(checkpoint_dir, "lcm_nfi_classified_present_vals.rds")

if (file.exists(lcm_classified_checkpoint) && file.exists(lcm_present_vals_checkpoint)) {

  cat("Loading lcm_nfi_classified from checkpoint...\n")
  lcm_nfi_classified <- rast(lcm_classified_checkpoint)
  present_vals <- readRDS(lcm_present_vals_checkpoint)

} else {

  cat("Rasterising NFI onto the same grid as the LCM classification...\n")

  t_nfi_rasterise <- system.time({
    nfi_national_raster <- rasterize(
      vect(nfi_urban), lcm_national_agg, field = 1, background = 0
    )
  })

  print(t_nfi_rasterise)

  # All woodland (LCM classes 1 and 2, plus any cell NFI flags) becomes a
  # single class, 1 "Woodland".
  lcm_nfi_classified <- lcm_national_agg
  lcm_nfi_classified[
    (lcm_national_agg %in% c(1, 2)) | (nfi_national_raster > 0)
  ] <- woodland_code

  present_vals <- sort(unique(values(lcm_nfi_classified, na.rm = TRUE)))

  cat("Saving checkpoint (", lcm_classified_checkpoint, ")...\n")
  writeRaster(lcm_nfi_classified, lcm_classified_checkpoint, overwrite = TRUE)
  saveRDS(present_vals, lcm_present_vals_checkpoint)

}

lcm_class_labels <- c(
  `1` = "Woodland",
  `3` = "Arable", `4` = "Improved grassland", `5` = "Neutral grassland",
  `6` = "Calcareous grassland", `7` = "Acid grassland",
  `8` = "Fen, marsh, swamp", `9` = "Heather", `10` = "Heather grassland",
  `11` = "Bog", `12` = "Inland rock", `13` = "Saltwater",
  `14` = "Freshwater", `15` = "Supra-littoral rock",
  `16` = "Supra-littoral sediment", `17` = "Littoral rock",
  `18` = "Littoral sediment", `19` = "Saltmarsh", `20` = "Urban",
  `21` = "Suburban"
)

# Explicit colours, grouped by land-cover family so that classes within a
# family are graded but distinct from the other families: greens for
# grassland, purples for heather, browns for wetland and bog, sandy tones
# for coastal sediment, greys for rock and urban, blues for water.
lcm_class_colours <- c(
  `1`  = "#1b5e20",  # Woodland -- dark green
  `3`  = "#d9a066",  # Arable -- tan/wheat
  `4`  = "#66bb6a",  # Improved grassland -- medium green
  `5`  = "#9ccc65",  # Neutral grassland -- yellow-green
  `6`  = "#c5e1a5",  # Calcareous grassland -- pale yellow-green
  `7`  = "#558b2f",  # Acid grassland -- olive green
  `8`  = "#6d4c41",  # Fen, marsh, swamp -- brown
  `9`  = "#8e44ad",  # Heather -- purple
  `10` = "#b39ddb",  # Heather grassland -- pale purple
  `11` = "#5d4037",  # Bog -- dark brown
  `12` = "#bfbfbf",  # Inland rock -- grey
  `13` = "#1565c0",  # Saltwater -- dark blue
  `14` = "#64b5f6",  # Freshwater -- light blue
  `15` = "#a6a6a6",  # Supra-littoral rock -- grey
  `16` = "#e0c9a6",  # Supra-littoral sediment -- sandy
  `17` = "#999999",  # Littoral rock -- grey
  `18` = "#f0e0b0",  # Littoral sediment -- pale sandy
  `19` = "#ce93d8",  # Saltmarsh -- pink-purple
  `20` = "#4d4d4d",  # Urban -- dark grey
  `21` = "#8c8c8c"   # Suburban -- medium grey
)

# Drop any value with no entry in lcm_class_labels (for example LCM's
# no-data value, often 0), so it does not appear as a blank legend swatch.
unlabelled_vals <- setdiff(present_vals, as.numeric(names(lcm_class_labels)))
if (length(unlabelled_vals) > 0) {
  cat(
    "WARNING: dropping", length(unlabelled_vals),
    "value(s) present in the data with no entry in lcm_class_labels:",
    paste(unlabelled_vals, collapse = ", "), "\n\n"
  )
  present_vals <- setdiff(present_vals, unlabelled_vals)
}

present_vals_chr <- as.character(present_vals)

plot(
  lcm_nfi_classified,
  type = "classes",
  levels = lcm_class_labels[present_vals_chr],
  col = lcm_class_colours[present_vals_chr],
  axes = FALSE,
  plg = list(cex = 0.6),
  main = "Land cover classification: LCM + NFI-patched woodland, England"
)

plot(vect(urban_regions_named), border = "black", lwd = 0.2, add = TRUE)

woodland_ha_check <- sum(values(lcm_nfi_classified) == woodland_code, na.rm = TRUE) *
  prod(res(lcm_nfi_classified)) / 10000

cat("\nTotal woodland (LCM + NFI union, whole cropped extent):",
    round(woodland_ha_check, 1), "ha\n")
```

# Same map, with Wales/Scotland/sea greyed out

The crop is a rectangular bounding box around all English urban regions,
so it also includes land cover for Wales and the southern edge of
Scotland. This masks everything outside England to a single grey
category, because the analysis is England only.

Uses the ONS "Countries (December 2022) Boundaries UK" dataset,
**BUC (ultra-generalised)** rather than BFC (full-resolution coastline).
BFC is a single very large multipart polygon (32 MB) that GDAL's GeoJSON
parser cannot read as one object, and a 200 m raster does not need its
precision.

```{r national_lcm_nfi_classified_england_only}
library(sf)

england_url <- paste0(
  "https://services1.arcgis.com/ESMARspQHYMw9BZ9/arcgis/rest/services/",
  "Countries_December_2022_UK_BUC/FeatureServer/0/query?",
  "where=CTRY22NM='England'&outFields=CTRY22NM&outSR=27700&f=geojson"
)

# Download to a local temp file rather than calling st_read() on the URL,
# which returns correct attributes but empty geometry for this service
# (the same problem as in fetch_nfi_bbox in 00_setup.R).
tmp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
download.file(england_url, tmp_file, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
england_boundary <- st_read(tmp_file, quiet = TRUE)
unlink(tmp_file)

outside_england_code <- 99

england_mask <- rasterize(vect(england_boundary), lcm_nfi_classified, field = 1, background = 0)

lcm_nfi_classified_england <- lcm_nfi_classified
lcm_nfi_classified_england[england_mask == 0] <- outside_england_code

lcm_class_labels_england <- c(lcm_class_labels, `99` = "Outside England")
lcm_class_colours_england <- c(lcm_class_colours, `99` = "grey80")
present_vals_england <- sort(unique(c(present_vals, outside_england_code)))
present_vals_england_chr <- as.character(present_vals_england)

plot(
  lcm_nfi_classified_england,
  type = "classes",
  levels = lcm_class_labels_england[present_vals_england_chr],
  col = lcm_class_colours_england[present_vals_england_chr],
  axes = FALSE,
  plg = list(cex = 0.6),
  main = "Land cover classification: LCM + NFI-patched woodland, England"
)

plot(vect(urban_regions_named), border = "black", lwd = 0.2, add = TRUE)
```

# National urban woodland (LCM + NFI union, masked to urban regions)

Derives a woodland/non-woodland boolean from `lcm_nfi_classified` (class
1), then masks it to the `urban_regions_named` shapes so that only
woodland inside a derived urban region remains. The classified map covers
the whole bounding box, including rural land between cities. The zoom
plots below use this layer.

```{r national_urban_woodland_map}
library(terra)

urban_regions_vect <- vect(urban_regions_named)

urban_woodland_national_unmasked <- lcm_nfi_classified == 1

cat("Masking combined woodland to the actual urban region shapes...\n\n")

t_mask <- system.time({
  urban_woodland_national <- mask(urban_woodland_national_unmasked, urban_regions_vect)
})

print(t_mask)

urban_woodland_ha <- sum(values(urban_woodland_national), na.rm = TRUE) *
  res(urban_woodland_national)[1] * res(urban_woodland_national)[2] / 10000

cat(
  "Total urban woodland (LCM + NFI union, masked to urban regions):",
  round(urban_woodland_ha, 1), "ha\n"
)

plot(
  urban_woodland_national,
  col = c("grey90", "darkgreen"),
  legend = FALSE,
  axes = FALSE,
  main = paste0(
    "Urban woodland only (LCM + NFI union), England (",
    agg_factor * 10, "m cells)"
  )
)
```

# Zoom: urban woodland in Milton Keynes and London

The national map above is aggregated to 200 m cells, which is too coarse
to show local detail. This rebuilds the same layer (LCM + NFI union,
masked to urban regions) at full 10 m resolution for one small bounding
box at a time, which is cheap because cropping happens before any heavy
computation.

```{r zoom_urban_woodland_mk_london}
library(terra)

zoom_bboxes <- list(
  "Milton Keynes" = st_bbox(
    c(xmin = 467500, ymin = 227500, xmax = 492500, ymax = 252500),
    crs = st_crs(27700)
  ),
  "London" = st_bbox(
    c(xmin = 495000, ymin = 150000, xmax = 565000, ymax = 205000),
    crs = st_crs(27700)
  )
)

# Masks against the target region's own geometry rather than every urban
# region in the padded bbox window, so unrelated neighbouring regions do
# not appear to be part of the same place.
plot_urban_woodland_zoom <- function(bbox, place_name, target_region) {

  bbox_sfc <- st_as_sfc(bbox)

  lcm_zoom <- rast(lcm_file) |> crop(vect(bbox_sfc))
  lcm_woodland_zoom <- lcm_zoom[[1]] %in% c(1, 2)

  # st_crop() on a polygon at the bbox edge can leave a degenerate sliver
  # (a point or line), which makes the result a mixed GEOMETRYCOLLECTION
  # that vect() cannot convert cleanly: it drops the geometry of the bad
  # rows but not their attribute rows. st_collection_extract("POLYGON")
  # keeps only the polygon parts and changes nothing for unaffected rows.
  nfi_zoom <- st_crop(nfi_urban, bbox) |>
    st_collection_extract("POLYGON")

  nfi_zoom_raster <- rasterize(
    vect(nfi_zoom), lcm_woodland_zoom, field = 1, background = 0
  )

  combined_zoom <- lcm_woodland_zoom | (nfi_zoom_raster > 0)

  target_geom <- st_crop(target_region, bbox) |>
    st_collection_extract("POLYGON")

  urban_woodland_zoom <- mask(combined_zoom, vect(target_geom))

  plot(
    urban_woodland_zoom,
    col = c("grey90", "darkgreen"),
    legend = FALSE,
    axes = FALSE,
    main = paste0("Urban woodland: ", place_name)
  )

  woodland_ha <- sum(values(urban_woodland_zoom), na.rm = TRUE) *
    res(urban_woodland_zoom)[1] * res(urban_woodland_zoom)[2] / 10000
  cat(place_name, "urban woodland:", round(woodland_ha, 1), "ha\n")

  invisible(urban_woodland_zoom)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))

for (place in names(zoom_bboxes)) {
  target_region <- urban_regions_named |> filter(bua_name == place)
  plot_urban_woodland_zoom(zoom_bboxes[[place]], place, target_region)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# Fetch ONS Major Towns and Cities boundaries

ONS Major Towns and Cities (December 2015, V2) boundaries: 112 named
towns and cities in England and Wales, built with the same Built-Up Areas
methodology as this project's regions. They identify the designated
places contained in each region. The data are already in EPSG:27700, and
112 features fit in one request (the page limit is 2,000), so no
pagination is needed.

```{r fetch_major_towns_cities}
library(sf)

tcity_url <- paste0(
  "https://services1.arcgis.com/ESMARspQHYMw9BZ9/arcgis/rest/services/",
  "Major_Towns_and_Cities_Dec_2015_Boundaries_V2_2022/FeatureServer/0/query",
  "?where=1=1&outFields=*&outSR=27700&f=geojson"
)

tmp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
utils::download.file(tcity_url, tmp_file, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
major_towns_cities <- st_read(tmp_file, quiet = TRUE)
unlink(tmp_file)

cat("Major Towns and Cities boundaries fetched:", nrow(major_towns_cities), "\n")
cat("CRS:", st_crs(major_towns_cities)$input, "\n")

saveRDS(
  major_towns_cities,
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "major_towns_cities.rds")
)
```

# Assign resistance values

`resistance_lookup` (Table 4.2 of the thesis; scale 1-10, higher is
harder for a typical urban woodland butterfly to cross) is defined in
`00_setup.R`. It is applied here to build the national 200 m resistance
surface for mapping; the per-region surfaces used for the connectivity
analysis are built in `03_National_ECS.Rmd`.

```{r assign_resistance_values}
library(terra)

if (!exists("lcm_nfi_classified")) {
  stop("lcm_nfi_classified not found. Run national_lcm_nfi_classified first.")
}

# resistance_lookup comes from 00_setup.R.
#
# others = NA: subst() leaves cell values not in `from` unchanged,
# including LCM's no-data value (0, sea or outside the crop). Left as 0
# they would plot as a real resistance bin; others = NA maps them to NA
# so they render as blank.
resistance_surface <- subst(
  lcm_nfi_classified,
  from = as.numeric(names(resistance_lookup)),
  to = as.numeric(resistance_lookup),
  others = NA
)

present_vals <- sort(unique(values(lcm_nfi_classified, na.rm = TRUE)))
missing_from_lookup <- setdiff(present_vals, as.numeric(names(resistance_lookup)))
if (length(missing_from_lookup) > 0) {
  cat(
    "WARNING: classes present in the data with no resistance value assigned",
    "(mapped to NA in resistance_surface, not a bug -- e.g. LCM's no-data",
    "sentinel, 0):", paste(missing_from_lookup, collapse = ", "), "\n\n"
  )
}

cat("Resistance surface built. Value summary:\n")
print(summary(values(resistance_surface)))

# Wales and Scotland get their own grey category (true sea stays NA and
# renders white). England's boundary is used as an exclusion test (is the
# cell outside England?) rather than using Wales and Scotland boundaries
# as an inclusion test. The England boundary is the generalised BUC
# version, whose simplified edges cut inside the true coastline in places.
# An inclusion test would leave coastal land showing in its original
# colour where the simplification cuts short, whereas an exclusion test
# only needs a cell to be clearly outside England.
if (!exists("england_mask")) {
  if (!exists("england_boundary")) {
    library(sf)
    england_url <- paste0(
      "https://services1.arcgis.com/ESMARspQHYMw9BZ9/arcgis/rest/services/",
      "Countries_December_2022_UK_BUC/FeatureServer/0/query?",
      "where=CTRY22NM='England'&outFields=CTRY22NM&outSR=27700&f=geojson"
    )
    tmp_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".geojson")
    download.file(england_url, tmp_file, quiet = TRUE, mode = "wb")
    england_boundary <- st_read(tmp_file, quiet = TRUE)
    unlink(tmp_file)
  }
  england_mask <- rasterize(vect(england_boundary), lcm_nfi_classified, field = 1, background = 0)
}

wales_scotland_code <- 99

lcm_nfi_classified_england <- lcm_nfi_classified
# Only recode cells that still hold a real land-cover value (not the
# literal 0 for no data or sea), otherwise true sea cells outside England
# would also be greyed out.
outside_england_real_land <- (england_mask == 0) & (lcm_nfi_classified_england != 0)
lcm_nfi_classified_england[outside_england_real_land] <- wales_scotland_code
# Anything still 0 at this point (true sea, or a few stray no-data cells
# inside England) becomes NA, so it renders as blank rather than taking a
# colour from the table below.
lcm_nfi_classified_england[lcm_nfi_classified_england == 0] <- NA

# Colours for this plot: forest green for Woodland alone; yellows and
# oranges for grassland and arable; two purples for heather and heather
# grassland; browns for fen, marsh, swamp and bog; teal for saltwater and
# blue for freshwater; dusty pink-mauve for saltmarsh; dark and medium
# grey for urban and suburban; muted tans and greys for rock and sediment.
resistance_plot_labels <- c(lcm_class_labels, `99` = "Wales / Scotland")
resistance_plot_colours <- c(
  `1`  = "#1b5e20",  # Woodland -- forest green
  `3`  = "#e8a33d",  # Arable -- orange
  `4`  = "#7cb342",  # Improved grassland -- yellow
  `5`  = "#e0c14c",  # Neutral grassland -- yellow
  `6`  = "#d4b83c",  # Calcareous grassland -- yellow
  `7`  = "#c9a227",  # Acid grassland -- deeper yellow/ochre
  `8`  = "#8d6e52",  # Fen, marsh, swamp -- brown
  `9`  = "#9575cd",  # Heather -- purple
  `10` = "#b39ddb",  # Heather grassland -- pale purple
  `11` = "#6d4c35",  # Bog -- brown
  `12` = "#b0a89a",  # Inland rock -- muted tan/grey
  `13` = "#2a9d8f",  # Saltwater -- teal
  `14` = "#4a90d9",  # Freshwater -- blue
  `15` = "#c2b8a3",  # Supra-littoral rock -- muted tan
  `16` = "#cabb9c",  # Supra-littoral sediment -- muted tan
  `17` = "#a89f91",  # Littoral rock -- muted grey
  `18` = "#d1c3a3",  # Littoral sediment -- muted tan
  `19` = "#c98fb0",  # Saltmarsh -- dusty pink-mauve
  `20` = "#4d4d4d",  # Urban -- dark grey
  `21` = "#8c8c8c",  # Suburban -- medium grey
  `99` = "grey85"    # Wales / Scotland
)
# Uses terra's built-in legend (plg =) rather than a custom legend()
# call, for reliable rendering. The trade-off is that the rock and
# sediment classes and "Outside England" also appear in the legend.
present_vals_england_classes <- sort(unique(values(lcm_nfi_classified_england, na.rm = TRUE)))
present_vals_england_classes_chr <- as.character(present_vals_england_classes)

plot(
  lcm_nfi_classified_england,
  type = "classes",
  levels = resistance_plot_labels[present_vals_england_classes_chr],
  col = resistance_plot_colours[present_vals_england_classes_chr],
  axes = FALSE,
  plg = list(cex = 0.7, title = "Surface type"),
  main = "Resistance surface, England"
)

plot(vect(urban_regions_named), border = "black", lwd = 0.2, add = TRUE)

saveRDS(
  resistance_lookup,
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "resistance_lookup.rds")
)

writeRaster(
  resistance_surface,
  file.path(checkpoint_dir, "resistance_surface.tif"),
  overwrite = TRUE
)

cat("\nSaved to:\n")
cat(" -", file.path(checkpoint_dir, "resistance_lookup.rds"), "\n")
cat(" -", file.path(checkpoint_dir, "resistance_surface.tif"), "\n")
```

# Zoom: resistance surface at native 10m resolution

The national map above is aggregated to 200 m cells for speed, which
understates urban woodland: most urban woodland is in small, sub-hectare
patches that a 4 ha (200 m) modal cell absorbs into "Urban" wherever
urban is more prevalent in the cell. This rebuilds the classified surface
(same LCM + NFI union rule and colours as `assign_resistance_values`
above) at native 10 m resolution for one small bounding box at a time,
which is cheap because cropping happens before any heavy computation. Use
it to check the national map or for figures that need local detail.

```{r zoom_resistance_surface}
library(terra)

plot_resistance_zoom <- function(bbox, place_name) {

  bbox_sfc <- st_as_sfc(bbox)

  lcm_zoom <- rast(lcm_file) |> crop(vect(bbox_sfc))

  nfi_zoom <- st_crop(nfi_urban, bbox) |> st_collection_extract("POLYGON")
  nfi_zoom_raster <- rasterize(vect(nfi_zoom), lcm_zoom[[1]], field = 1, background = 0)

  woodland_code <- 1
  lcm_zoom_classified <- lcm_zoom[[1]]
  lcm_zoom_classified[
    (lcm_zoom[[1]] %in% c(1, 2)) | (nfi_zoom_raster > 0)
  ] <- woodland_code
  lcm_zoom_classified[lcm_zoom_classified == 0] <- NA

  present_vals_zoom <- sort(unique(values(lcm_zoom_classified, na.rm = TRUE)))
  present_vals_zoom_chr <- as.character(present_vals_zoom)

  plot(
    lcm_zoom_classified,
    type = "classes",
    levels = resistance_plot_labels[present_vals_zoom_chr],
    col = resistance_plot_colours[present_vals_zoom_chr],
    axes = FALSE,
    plg = list(cex = 0.7, title = "Surface type"),
    main = paste0("Resistance surface -- ", place_name, " (native 10m)")
  )
  plot(vect(urban_regions_named), border = "black", lwd = 0.4, add = TRUE)

  woodland_ha <- sum(values(lcm_zoom_classified) == woodland_code, na.rm = TRUE) *
    prod(res(lcm_zoom_classified)) / 10000
  cat(place_name, "woodland (native 10m):", round(woodland_ha, 1), "ha\n")

  invisible(lcm_zoom_classified)
}

london_bbox <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = 495000, ymin = 150000, xmax = 565000, ymax = 205000),
  crs = st_crs(27700)
)

plot_resistance_zoom(london_bbox, "London")
```
